articles.title: Sonora Rally Evolves for 2027 with Three-Day Format And Rally Schools
articles.summary: Route planning for adventure motorcycles sits right between logistics and art. A good route doesn’t just connect points on a map—it shapes the entire experience, manages your risk, and determines whether a trip becomes a highlight reel or an expensive recovery story. In this episode of our ADV 101 series, we break down how to plan sustainable, epic backcountry adventure rides. From calculating true "time to traverse" instead of relying on mileage to land access regulations, weather extremes, bailout options, and using paper maps alongside GPS tools like Gaia, onX, and Garmin Tread. Check out the written article here: https://www.motorcycle.com/bikes/how-to/adv-101-the-art-of-route-planning-44668846 Thanks to Yamaha Motor Corporation USA for sponsoring this video. Learn more at www.yamahamotorsports.com For 2025, Aprilia didn't reinvent the wheel — they refined the standard 659cc parallel-twin with Euro 5+ compliance and punchier low-gear fueling. Then, they dropped the Rally Edition: a package that's ready to rock equipped with factory armor, narrower tubeless wheels, a titanium SC-Project exhaust, and linear-rate KYB fork springs. We put the Aprilia Tuareg Rally through its paces to see if the $1,500 factory upgrade is worth your hard-earned cash.
articles.body:
The Sonora Rally is hoping to make it easier for new riders and racers to take part in the event.

Sonora Rally Evolves for 2027 with a New Three-Day Format and Expanded Rally Schools Built for Everyone from First-Time Navigators to Dakar-Bound Racers

For 13 years, Sonora Rally has given competitors a place to discover what rally raid really demands. Navigation. Endurance. Independence. A roadbook, an odometer, a machine, and enough open desert to find out whether all four-and the person behind the wheel or handlebars-can work together. Now, in 2027, Sonora Rally is making that experience easier to reach without making the rally itself easy.

The 2027 Sonora Rally, February 11–14, introduces a streamlined three-day rally raid based from a single bivouac in the San Luis Río Colorado region of Sonora, Mexico. Competitors unpack once, establish one home base, and race from there-reducing the expense, time, and moving logistics traditionally associated with rally raid while preserving the navigation, terrain, competition, and adventure that have defined Sonora for more than a decade. It is, quite simply, fewer logistics and more rally.

Just south of the U.S.–Mexico border, San Luis Río Colorado also puts the event within easy reach of competitors traveling from the United States, Canada, and Mexico. International racers can connect through San Diego, Phoenix, Mexicali, or Mexico City, while Fly-N-Race Moto and UTV rental and support programs offer another option for competitors who would rather arrive ready to race than haul an entire program across the continent.

And before February ever arrives, Sonora is opening the desert for something else: learning how to race it.

The Sonora Rally Schools return December 4–6, 2026, with an expanded format designed around a simple reality: not everyone who comes to Sonora needs the same training.

For Baja racers, desert riders, UTV competitors, and newcomers curious about making the jump into rally raid, the Navigation School combines classroom instruction with practical dune navigation. It offers first-timers a foundation in roadbook racing while giving developing competitors the opportunity to sharpen their navigation before returning to race Sonora in February.

Learn navigation in December. Race Sonora in February.

For experienced rally racers and Dakar-bound competitors, the Advanced Route removes the classroom altogether. Challenging Dakar-style roadbooks put the emphasis on seat time, navigation, and training in the dunes-a chance to prepare for Dakar or sharpen the tools required for Sonora 2027.

This year also introduces an entirely new option: a one-day Dunes Clinic led by ZXMoto Joyride Factory rider, multi-year Dakar veteran and former Sonora Rally Road to Dakar winner Skyler Howes, alongside Sonora Rally organizer and Dakar veteran Darren Skilton.

Limited to only eight vehicles, the clinic offers a focused day of hands-on big-dune training ahead of the weekend schools. For competitors accustomed to speed but less accustomed to reading large dunes, momentum and terrain, it offers an opportunity to learn from two people whose experience was earned in precisely those environments.

The objective across all three programs is not to make rally raid simple. It is to make learning it more accessible.

The rally may be shorter in 2027. The opportunity is not.

As North America's only official Road to Dakar event, Sonora Rally continues to offer competitors a pathway toward the sport's biggest stage.

In the UTV Road to Dakar, the winning eligible team will receive a paid entry into the 2028 Dakar Rally, a prize valued at more than $33,000 USD.*

For motorcycles, eligible competitors who finish the 2027 Sonora Rally will earn six Dakar eligibility points toward Dakar 2028.*

The new format therefore changes the commitment required to reach the starting line-not what waits on the other side of it.

From a first roadbook to a Dakar campaign, Sonora Rally is building a clearer path into rally raid. Come to learn. Come to train. Come to race. And for those with considerably bigger ideas, come find out where the roadbook can take you.

Dunes Clinic • Navigation School • Advanced Training

2027 SONORA RALLY - THREE-DAY RALLY RAID

Special incentives available for the first 20 entries.

articles.title: Cowboys-Bucs live discussion: An MVP candidate versus a rookie quarterback
articles.summary: The Cowboys take on the Bucs on Thursday night football
articles.body:
No Baker Mayfield last week for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That meant rookie Jalon Daniels took the reins. Daniels went 9-for-27 for 148 yards, threw two interceptions, posted a 65 passer rating, and was sacked three times.

The San Francisco 49ers play the Dallas Cowboys a month from now. In my opinion, that's an NFC Championship preview.

But the Cowboys won't win a playoff game if their 32nd-ranked defense in EPA per play doesn't improve. And it's not as if teams are gashing the Cowboys, which would inflate their defensive numbers. They're dead last in success rate, too.

Something has to give on that side of the ball. There's only one way for Daniels to go. Without Joey Porter Jr., Dallas has been more than accommodating to opposing offenses. He's not in uniform tonight.

Dak Prescott has been surgical this season. Only Brock Purdy and Lamar Jackson have generated a higher EPA. Prescott has an 8-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Historically, he's been aggressive against the blitz. That does not bode well for a Todd Bowles defense. It could be a long night for a Tampa Bay secondary without Antoine Winfield.

My gut says 31-14, Cowboys. But this is not a team that wins comfortably. Their defense won't allow it. So I'll go 28-24 in an exciting Thursday showdown.

articles.title: Athlete of the Week: Blake Shaffer
articles.summary: lake Shaffer started playing football at a young age. He continued that into high school where he has showed out for the Rifle Bears.
articles.body:
RIFLE, Colo. ( KREX ) - Blake Shaffer started playing football at a young age. He continued that into high school where he has showed out for the Rifle Bears.

"It's like the chess of sports," Shaffer said. "The contact, Friday Night Lights, you can just go out and hit someone and it feels great scoring touchdowns."

He started football in third grade. Shaffer was a running back in his early days before switching and playing more receiver and tight end. A wrestler as well, Shaffer prefers football and said he made is favorite memory this year.

"It feels great getting long runs and you can hear the crowd," he said. "Coal Ridge this year, we were down two touchdowns and then I got that one touchdown to bring us to one touchdown and it just felt great hearing the crowd."

That touchdown and the win over Coal Ridge helped set the tone for the season. Shaffer had a big performance and has continued that play all year.

"You could tell it was more hype," Shaffer said about the win over Coal Ridge. "We felt good to win because from the last two years we didn't really feel it a lot. It just kept pushing us because we wanted to keep winning after that."

Shaffer made the switch to running back for Rifle coming into the season. Throw in a brand new playbook and he had plenty to work on coming into the year. He has handled it all in stride.

"Practicing running back and going into camp and everything I was like, 'Yeah, I really, I love this position,'" he said. "My senior year I really wanted to pop off and play with my brothers under the lights."

He has popped off in a big way. He has three games with over 200 yards. In his past two games he has five touchdowns and 470 total yards.

"It's been great," he said. "As a team, we're a lot closer, it's more of a brotherhood. I think because we all got the new playbook together, we all had to learn it together and I really feel like it brought us even closer because we just had to learn it together and go through our ups and downs together."

Shaffer thanked his parents, coaches and teammates for their support. He shouted his teammate Cache Garcia and his offensive line for their play.

articles.title: Bears running game looms as huge factor vs. Packers — but will Kyle Monangai play?
articles.summary: CHICAGO — When it comes to the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers, you can never take any statistical advantage as a given. But there’s one phase of the gam...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — When it comes to the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers, you can never take any statistical advantage as a given. But there's one phase of the game — at least on paper — the Bears seem to have the Packers over a barrel: the running game.

The Bears enter Sunday's Week 5 matchup at Lambeau Field boasting the No. 1 rushing offense at 196.3 yards per game. Conversely, the Packers run defense ranks 28th, allowing 139.3 yards per game.

However, Bears running backs coach Eric Studesville doesn't see a vulnerability at all.

"The (defensive) front is impressive," he said. "The backers are really impressive. I think (linebacker) Zaire Franklin's a good addition for them. (Linebacker Edgerrin) Cooper going down (with a torn Achilles) is different, but (Isaiah) McDuffie's going to be in there. He's going to play his tail off.

"The safeties (Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney) and the nickel (Javon Bullard) are really good players, and so I think this day is going to be a great challenge for us. But if we go and do what we're supposed to do, we'll have a chance."

Bears running backs Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift rank seventh and eighth among the league's rushing leaders with 324 and 311 yards, respectively.

Monangai ranks sixth among qualifiers with 5.4 yards per carry.

According to Next Gen Stats, Monangai reaches the line of scrimmage in just 2.50 seconds on average, the fastest mark among 39 running backs with at least 30 carries.

"He's aggressive and decisive," Studesville said. "He's a vertical cut, but he's a tough, physical runner, runs behind his pads. He brings a physicality to our offense, and that gives us juice."

On a 30-carry, 146-yard day against the New York Jets, Monangai had 106 yards after contact — the fifth-highest mark in a game this season, behind two runs apiece from the Atlanta Falcons' Bijan Robinson and Kansas City Chiefs' Kenneth Walker — and three runs of at least 10 yards.

After Swift fumbled in the third quarter, Monangai finished with 19 carries for 96 yards, including a 26-yarder, and a touchdown.

"Happy for him," Swift said Thursday. "He finished the game how he's supposed to. Had a hell of a game."

The hiccup for Week 5 is that Monangai missed a second consecutive day of practice Thursday with thumb and toe injuries. Coach Ben Johnson said earlier this week that the thumb injury shouldn't be an issue, but he hadn't addressed Monangai's toe injury.

Swift was limited in practice with hip and knee injuries. He had 15 carries for 58 yards against the Jets, but the biggest blemish of his day was the lost fumble, his second of the season.

"That ain't me," Swift said. "So I'm not about to make it a thing. Just be more conscious of it."

Another flaw for the Bears has been their lack of effectiveness in the red zone (42.11%, ranked 30th), an area of emphasis all week. But red-zone rushing probably has been particularly galling for Ben Johnson, as big a disciple of the run as there is in the league.

In the first series against the Jets, Swift saw touchdown runs from the 3- and 1-yard lines reversed on replay. The Bears turned the ball over on downs.

On the next series, the Bears drove to the Jets 4, but it took three straight tries for Monangai to cross the goal line.

"Very" frustrating, Swift said. "Because I think if we clean up the red-zone scoring we'll be in a better position offensively with points and things like that. But got to get it in there. Got to score on the first drive."

Swifts other fumble this season also came in the red zone: He fumbled near the goal line against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

The Bears converted 100% of red-zone trips against the Panthers, but the fact they went 0 for 3 against the Vikings and converted 40% versus the Philadelphia Eagles and 29% against the Jets over the last three weeks has been "disappointing," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said.

"Certain teams have played us maybe a little bit differently than we planned for based on whatever they saw on us," he said. "So we're trying to make sure we do a great job self-scouting, things like that.

"But ultimately it's something we got to get cleaned up, and I think we're on the right track of doing that. But it's got to show up for us."

Guards Jonah Jackson (ankle) and Joe Thuney (pectoral) and right tackle Darnell Wright (ankle) all returned to practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session.

Quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) missed practice.

However, defensive backs Kyler Gordon (calf) and Cam Lewis (hip) were full participants, as were linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles) and Shemar Turner (knee).

Gordon, Sewell and Turner remained on the reserve/physically unable to perform list as of Thursday but have been practicing in their respective 21-day return-to-pay windows.

articles.title: #1 Huskers Sweep #15 Indiana
articles.summary: The Huskers stay on top behind strong performances from Harper Murray and Teraya Sigler
articles.body:
It was an early evening top 25 showdown for the Huskers and the Hoosiers. Nebraska came out hot in the first set and carried that out into the second. Indiana kept set three much closer before the Huskers pulled away in the end.

Harper Murray led all hitters with 11 kills after having only 1 kill in the first set, she also had one ace, seven digs, and two blocks. Teraya Sigler was right behind her with 10 kills and two blocks. Mania Ogbechie had eight kills and six blocks while hitting .500. Olivia Mach had 10 kills and three service aces.

The Huskers hit a .379 on the night, allowing Indiana to hit .282, higher than what they typically allow.

Coach Dani Busboom Kelly added a new look that we hadn't seen before. She had both Mania Ogbechie and Kenna Cogill playing front row at the same time late in the match to help the Husker block. It definitely paid off.

The Huskers started off the match with a behind the setter kill from Mania Ogbechie, followed by an Andi Jackson kill. Bergan Reilly spread the offense out and the Huskers first five points came from kills from five different hitters. The Huskers got out to an early 8-2 lead. Indiana battled back a few points with an ace and tooling the block. The Huskers led going into the media time out 15-9. Bergan Reilly came out of the time out and threw down two kills. The Huskers were first to 20, however Indiana started to come alive with their block. The Huskers end the set with a big block themselves.

Nebraska hit .375 while holding Indiana to .179. Teraya Sigler led all hitters with 5 kills on the set.

Olivia Mauch served the Huskers first ace of the match putting the Huskers up 2-1. Both teams were picking up a lot off the floor for a long rally with Virginia Adriano seeing a lot of action and finally killing the ball. Laney Choboy got her 20th ace of the season to put the Huskers up 7-2. After a phantom net call on Andi Jackson that was challenged and somehow stood, the Huskers were the first to 15, leading 15-11. This was a set of challenges as both teams challenged a block touch and won their challenges. Harper Murray made some smart shots and gave the Huskers some crucial kills down the line, including a back row bomb to end the set.

The Huskers hit .400 in the second set, but allowed Indiana to hit .333.

Both teams added two blocks in this set making them tied at 4 each.

Indiana starts off the set on 2-0 run. After a few errors, the Huskers even up the score 3-3 with a solid block. The Huskers go on a 5-0 run with Harper Murray behind the service line. Teraya Sigler and Andi Jackson had some monster kills and Murray added another ace. Laney Choboy and Olivia Mauch were digging everything in that run as well. A few Husker errors and Hoosier kills even up the score at 10. An Ogbechie kill ends a 4-0 run for Indiana. Mauch gets two more aces to give the Huskers the lead again 14-13. Once again the Huskers go on a run with Harper Murray behind the service line. There was a rally that had Murray saving the ball while running all the way into the bench, and then coming back to put the point away with a back row crusher. Once again the Huskers were the first to 20. In an interesting wrinkle, DBK puts Kenna Cogill in the front row while keeping Ogbechie in too and they sealed the match with two blocks.

While the Huskers started the set off with quite a few uncharacteristic errors, the rallied and ended set three hitting .357.

The Huskers next game is a Saturday night black out against Wisconsin at Bob Devaney sports center at 6pm.
